# Dry run, 2026-11-17: five North Carolina places

**What ran.** The full swarm (worklist → scout → primary and blind coders → check → verifier → rows →
hand-off), with the main session as orchestrator, on Raleigh (3755000), Greensboro (3728000), Wilmington
(3774440), Asheville (3702140) and Matthews (3741960). State law was skipped (NC S.L. 2026-59 rows already
exist and are generated separately). The agent files were used as prompts for general-purpose subagents,
because new agent types load only when a session starts. Run folder, outside the repo:
`~/lotline-data/rule_agents/adu/NC/dryrun-2026-11-17/` (sources, codings, decisions, final, `rows.csv`,
`tasks.csv`, `tasks.md`, `compare.txt`). No model, engine or scenario script was run; nothing in `config/`
changed; the coders and verifier were told not to open `config/reforms/`, the research sheets or the logbook.

**Why these places.** All five are already coded in `config/reforms/nc.csv`, mostly second-coded
(WS-ADU-RULES, 2026-11-12). Together they cover what the swarm has to handle: rich official PDFs (Raleigh),
a Cloudflare-walled city site (Greensboro), Municode-only code plus a 2021 code rewrite (Wilmington),
code-only-on-Municode with a recent change (Asheville), and a town whose robots.txt disallows agents
(Matthews).

## Result against the coded rows

`compare` matches eras by effective year; 62 field comparisons:

| outcome | count | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| match | 34 | same value (dates, by right, owner occupancy, detached, size, parking, ADUs per lot) |
| differs | 1 | Wilmington 2021 adoption date: swarm 2021-08-01 (month only, from news), coded 2021-08-17 |
| swarm blank | 18 | the swarm would not code from what it could read (mirror-only, blocked code, judgment call) |
| existing blank | 1 | Wilmington 2012 adoption date (swarm has 2012-08-21; coded row leaves it blank) |
| era on one side only | 8 | see below |

Not one value the swarm coded contradicts a coded row. It is conservative: 18 fields left blank, and every
one of them is now a human lookup with a URL.

**Eras on one side only, one by one.**
- Raleigh 2013 and 2019 vs swarm "2016 [predates], no ADUs". Existing: a 2013 "no ADU" row, then the 2019
  cottage-overlay ordinance (TC-3-17) coded `adus_per_lot = 1`, `by_right = False`. Both swarm coders, on
  their own, coded the overlay-by-petition period as **no ADUs** (lessons L-F1: units only through a
  rezoning are "none"). **Judgment call for Ben** (below).
- Raleigh 2022 (Missing Middle 2.0, TC-20-21: size bands) and Wilmington 2022 (O-2022-41/88: cap 900 →
  1,200): **missed by both coders**. The scout did not list these amendments, so neither coder looked. Fix
  applied: an explicit amendment sweep in the scout (`rules-adu-scout.md` step 3).
- Greensboro 2017 vs swarm 2016: the same rule, dated differently. The coded row uses the LDO's 2017
  printing as `[earliest-known]`; the swarm, with no first date, dated it `[predates]` at 2016-01-01 (the
  WS-ADU-RULES convention 6). Values not compared because the years differ; the coded row has owner
  occupancy and one parking space, the swarm left both blank (the old LDO is behind Greensboro's bot wall).
- Asheville 2026 (new): both coders found a 2026-08-25 change (ADUs by right, 1,000 sq ft, no parking),
  read on Zoneomics and the city's page only, so `medium` and `DATE UNCONFIRMED`. Not in config. A **lead**
  for Ben, with a lookup task to confirm it on the official code.
- Matthews: no rows. The town's robots.txt disallows agents and nothing official was found elsewhere; the
  coded row (2016, from Municode) stands. Two lookups were queued.

## What the dry run found in the swarm itself (all fixed and tested in this PR)

1. **Scanned-PDF check was wrong** for modern PDFs (fonts hidden in compressed object streams): Raleigh and
   Wilmington text PDFs were flagged as scans. Now inflates streams with zlib. Test added.
2. **Wayback year drift**: `/web/2023/<url>` silently served a 2025 capture. The fetch result now returns
   `final_url` and `wayback_ts`; coders cite those. Test added.
3. **Archived official pages were labelled `mirror`**, which caps confidence. Rule added: an archived page
   keeps its kind, with `archived_from`.
4. **"Before" eras dated on the reform day**: coders used `in_force_by <reform date>` for the state before
   a reform, so the resolver put the old era on the reform's date. New date type `prior_to` (start unknown →
   `[predates]` at the window start). Test added.
5. **Coders set date tags inconsistently** (`[predates]` on a rule with a 2015 vote date). Date-quality tags
   are now set only by the resolver; `check` rejects coder-set ones. Test added.
6. **Unknown block reasons and fields** (`not_tried_known_blocker`, `all`) crashed the task step. `check` now
   validates both; `known_blocker` reason added; `all` expands to every field. Tests added.
7. **Too many lookups**: 31 tasks (310 min) before; merging by place + page and dropping fields the verifier
   already settled on primary evidence gives 20 (200 min). Test added. The hand-off agent (Sonnet, 100k
   tokens) then merged 8 more and rewrote questions, look-fors and estimates: **12 lookups, 165 minutes**,
   the largest a 15-minute version-history hunt, the smallest a 5-minute judgment call (Raleigh's lot-size
   tiered cap).
8. **Missing amendments** (above): amendment sweep added to the scout; budget raised to 8 searches and 10
   fetches per place.
9. **No PDF text tool** in the environment: the Read tool could not open PDFs here (no poppler), and the
   coders compiled a throwaway macOS PDFKit extractor in their scratchpad to read and check quotes. That works
   but is not reproducible on Linux or in CI. **Decision for Ben:** add `pypdf` (BSD-3-Clause).

I relabelled the dry-run codings for fixes 4–6 by script (originals kept in `coding_*_v1/`), so the verifier
and the comparison ran on the new rules: `in_force_by` → `prior_to` on "before" eras the coders had tagged
`[predates]`, coder-set date tags removed, `not_tried_known_blocker` → `known_blocker`. No value was changed.

## Cost

Subagent tokens: scout 107k (Sonnet), primary coder 214k, blind coder 394k, verifier 138k, hand-off packager
100k (Sonnet). About 1.0M tokens for five places, roughly 200k per place, against 77k per place for the
October MN metro run, which found statuses for only 52 of 162 places. The blind coder costs the most;
`--no-second-coder` (D-088) roughly halves a run.

## Verdict

The pipeline works end to end, and its output is schema-valid `reforms` rows. On the fields it coded, it
agrees with the second-coded rows. Its main weakness was finding later amendments, which is now addressed
in the scout. Its main cost is the blind coder. Rows from this run are **not** proposed for `config/`: the
existing NC rows are more complete for these five places.
